rows.scope: Solve word problems involving addition of three whole numbers with a sum at most 20; represent the situation using objects, drawings, or equations with an unknown-number symbol.
Use properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract, including commutativity of addition and associativity of addition; students need not use formal property names.
Interpret subtraction as an unknown-addend problem; find a missing addend that completes an addition equation to determine a difference.
Connect counting with addition and subtraction, including counting on to add.
Understand the meaning of the equal sign; determine whether addition and subtraction equations are true or false, including equations with nonstandard placement or expressions on both sides.
Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers, including an unknown in different positions.
Count to 120 beginning at any number less than 120; read and write numerals in that range and represent a number of objects with a written numeral.
Compare two two-digit numbers using the place values of their tens and ones digits and record comparisons using >, =, and <.

Add within 100, including two-digit plus one-digit and two-digit plus a multiple of 10, using concrete models or drawings and place-value, operation-property, or addition/subtraction-relationship strategies; connect strategies to written methods and explain reasoning; combine tens with tens and ones with ones, sometimes composing a ten.
Given a two-digit number, mentally determine 10 more and 10 less without counting, and explain the reasoning.

Subtract a multiple of 10 between 10 and 90 from a multiple of 10 between 10 and 90, with a positive or zero result; use concrete models or drawings and place value, properties, or addition/subtraction relationships, connect strategies to written methods, and explain the reasoning.
Order three objects by length and compare the lengths of two objects indirectly using a third object.
Tell and write time in hours and half-hours using both analog and digital clocks.
Organize, represent, and interpret data with up to three categories; answer questions about total data points, category counts, and how many more or fewer are in one category than another.

Distinguish defining shape attributes, such as being closed and three-sided, from nondefining features such as color, orientation, and overall size; build and draw shapes having specified defining attributes.

Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, quarter-circles) or three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, right circular cylinders) into composite shapes, then compose new shapes from the composite shapes; formal solid names are not required.
